skill.name: simplify
skill.description: Simplify and refine recently modified code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability without changing behavior.
skill.summary: Refines recent code changes to improve readability while preserving exact functionality.
skill.author: brianlovin

content.value_statement: Code changes often collect extra complexity during implementation. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code refine recent edits for clarity without changing behavior.
actual_capabilities: Reviews recently modified code for readability and maintainability issues.
Applies project coding standards such as import style, naming, and component structure.
Reduces unnecessary nesting, redundant logic, and overly clever expressions.
Preserves existing functionality while improving code structure.
Removes obvious comments when the code is already clear.
Documents only significant simplifications that affect understanding.
limitations: It depends on the agent having access to the recent code changes.
It does not replace a full security review or bug audit.
It may need project tests to confirm behavior is unchanged.
It focuses on recent changes unless asked to inspect a broader scope.

use_cases.title: Clean up a feature branch
use_cases.description: Refine a finished implementation before review by reducing unnecessary complexity and improving naming.

use_cases.title: Apply team code style
use_cases.description: Bring recent edits closer to local conventions for imports, React components, functions, and error handling.

use_cases.title: Prepare safer AI-generated code
use_cases.description: Review AI-written changes and make them more explicit, readable, and maintainable before merging.

prompt_templates.title: Simplify my latest changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the simplify skill to review my recent edits and improve readability without changing behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request after completing a small code change

prompt_templates.title: Clean up this branch before review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the simplify skill on the current branch. Keep functionality the same and focus on clarity, naming, and project style.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a specific area
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the simplify skill on the recent changes in the authentication flow. Preserve behavior and avoid broad unrelated refactors.

prompt_templates.title: Balance simplification with maintainability
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the simplify skill to reduce complexity, but keep helpful abstractions and avoid dense one-line code or nested ternaries.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup where readability matters more than line count

output_examples.input: Recent edits added repeated conditional branches and unclear variable names.
output_examples.output: The skill would consolidate related logic, rename variables for intent, and keep explicit branches when they improve readability.

output_examples.input: A React component was changed with inline prop shapes and mixed import ordering.
output_examples.output: The skill would align imports, prefer explicit props types, and preserve the component behavior.

output_examples.input: A helper function became shorter but harder to understand.
output_examples.output: The skill would prefer clear structure over brevity and avoid clever expressions that make debugging harder.

best_practices: Run tests after simplification to confirm behavior stayed the same.
Use it after implementation, before code review, when context is still fresh.
Give a clear scope so the agent avoids unrelated cleanup.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a substitute for bug finding or security review.
Do not ask it to minimize line count at the expense of clarity.
Do not apply broad refactors when only recent changes need cleanup.

faq.question: Does this skill change program behavior?
faq.answer: No. Its stated goal is to preserve exact functionality while improving clarity and consistency.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it after writing or modifying code, especially before opening a pull request.

faq.question: Does it review for bugs?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on quality, readability, and maintainability, not deep correctness or security analysis.

faq.question: Can it work across an entire repository?
faq.answer: It can be asked to review a broader scope, but its default focus is recently modified code.

faq.question: What tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How should I verify the result?
faq.answer: Review the diff and run the relevant tests or application checks for the changed code.
